cards.explanation: The answer is that His face shines like the sun. Matthew says, "His face shone like the sun…" Peter, James and John saw it right in front of them. I'd have needed oven mitts for my eyeballs.

The answer is Moses and Elijah. "Suddenly Moses and Elijah appeared before them, talking with Jesus." Moses was Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), and Elijah was a prophet (1 Kings 18:36). Two giants from Israel's long past, and they just show up on a mountaintop. Friends, I'd need a minute to sit down.

The answer is False. Moses and Elijah are not silent statues. The text says they appeared "…talking with Jesus." Picture a quiet mountaintop where three people are having a conversation, and Peter, James and John get to watch.

The answer is three shelters. Peter says, "…I will put up three shelters…" One for Jesus, one for Moses and one for Elijah. The man is offering to do construction in the middle of a miracle, and I respect the energy.

The answer is "My beloved Son." The voice from the cloud says, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!" It speaks about Jesus and calls Him Son. It's the clearest introduction on the whole mountain.

The answer is listen. The voice says, "Listen to Him!" Peter was still speaking when the cloud wrapped around them. I talk a LOT, so I take that line personally. Good news is, it's a fine thing to practice, friends.

The answer is True. Matthew says, "When the disciples heard this, they fell facedown in terror." They had just heard a voice from the cloud. I dive face first into chocolate chips for fun, but they hit the ground out of terror.
The answer is afraid. Jesus says, "Get up… Do not be afraid." He touched them first, and then He spoke. The three of them had just fallen facedown in terror, so I think that touch meant a lot.
The answer is False. Moses and Elijah are not still standing there. The text says, "…they saw no one except Jesus." After all that glow, cloud and voice, it ends with Jesus, right there with them.

The answer is until He is raised from the dead. Jesus says, "Do not tell anyone about this vision until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead." That's the timeline He gives Peter, James and John. I can't hold a secret for five minutes, so I'm impressed, friends.
The answer is False. Jesus says, "Elijah does indeed come, and he will restore all things." He doesn't say the scribes have it mixed up. Then He adds that Elijah has already come.

The answer is suffer. Jesus says, "In the same way, the Son of Man will suffer at their hands." I think this one is heavy, so I'll keep it simple. Back in verse 9 He also mentions being raised from the dead, so both are part of what He says.

The answer is John the Baptist. The text says, "Then the disciples understood that He was speaking to them about John the Baptist." John the Baptist came preaching in the Desert of Judea (Matthew 3:1). The lightbulb goes off right there on the mountain path.
